chung.Description:
This course provides a comprehensive examination of the rapidly evolving digital marketplace through the tripartite lens of business, technology, and society. It establishes a theoretical framework for understanding how digital trade mechanisms have revolutionized traditional economic structures and continue to reshape global commerce.

In this course, students will investigate the foundational elements of the digital economy, ranging from technical infrastructures and security protocols to complex business models. The curriculum requires learners to analyze critical strategies in digital marketing and supply chain management while simultaneously evaluating the ethical, social, and political implications inherent in online commerce. Through this rigorous inquiry, participants engage with the practical realities of online retail, content delivery, and collaborative commerce.

Upon completion, participants will possess the analytical acumen necessary to evaluate diverse e-commerce initiatives and the technical insight required for establishing a robust digital presence. Graduates will emerge equipped with a strategic perspective that integrates commercial innovation with ethical responsibility, preparing them to effectively navigate and lead within the complexities of the global digital trade environment.

taiLieu: Kenneth C. Laudon and Carol G. Traver
clo: Distinguish the fundamental business models and technological infrastructures of e-commerce to explain how they generate value and competitive advantage in the digital marketplace.
Interpret the essential principles of digital marketing, supply chain management, and online retail strategies to identify their roles in driving business growth and operational efficiency.
Apply basic business analysis frameworks to evaluate the usability, commercial viability, and customer experience of existing e-commerce websites and mobile platforms.
Analyze the managerial implications of security risks and payment systems to propose appropriate non-technical strategies for risk mitigation and consumer trust building.
Cultivate a professional awareness of legal compliance and ethical responsibility to address social and political issues arising within the digital trade environment.
danhGia: Chapter 1-12 of book E-commerce 2023-2024: business, technology, society (18th edition)

Group Project: The E-commerce Go-to-Market Strategy

This group project requires students to simulate the role of a digital management team launching a new product or transitioning an existing physical product into the online marketplace. The objective is to synthesize the theoretical knowledge from the course into a cohesive, actionable business plan. Student groups should select a tangible consumer product and develop a four-stage strategy that covers the lifecycle of an e-commerce transaction, from product conceptualization to post-sales retention.

Project Requirements and Structure
- Stage 1: Product Selection and Business Model Definition
- Stage 2: Platform Selection and Infrastructure Strategy
- Stage 3: Digital Marketing and Customer Acquisition
- Stage 4: Post-Sales Operations and Customer Retention

Deliverable The group will present their strategy in a 20-minute presentation followed by a Q&A session. The presentation should clearly demonstrate the logical connection between the chosen product, the selected technology, and the managerial decisions made throughout the planning process.

Each team will discuss in advance with the lecturer about the suitability of the project

The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark.

Group size: 5-6 members
Chapter 6 - 8 of book E-commerce 2023-2024: business, technology, society (18th edition)

Time Allotted: 90 Minutes
Format: Individual Written Memorandum (500–700 words)
Title: Integrated Digital Strategy and Ethics Audit

This in-class individual assignment requires the student to assume the role of a strategic consultant analyzing a specific e-commerce retailer within a ninety-minute timeframe. The student should first examine the firm's marketing and advertising mechanisms by identifying specific deployments of behavioral targeting or personalization strategies to assess their effectiveness in customer acquisition. Following this analysis, the student should evaluate the integration of social, mobile, and local marketing initiatives to determine how well the firm leverages these platforms for community engagement and seamless user experiences. Concluding the audit, the student should conduct a critical risk assessment regarding information rights and data privacy, utilizing ethical frameworks to recommend strategic improvements that balance commercial objectives with strict consumer protection standards.

- In-class performance of student;
- Case-study participation

Individual assignments are graded on a scale of 0-10, precise to one digit after the decimal, which will be contingent upon their participation and fulfill the other's requirements of the lecturer (can be homework, inclass excercise...).
